title: Mining with FP-Growth
note: FP-Growth builds a compressed prefix tree of the baskets and finds frequent itemsets without generating candidates, unlike Apriori. Both are run in the benchmark and must return identical itemsets. Rules with lift ≤ 1 are dropped: they say A makes B less likely, not more.

title: Out-of-sample validation + FDR
note: Every rule is re-measured on held-out baskets. A one-sided Fisher exact test asks whether B is over-represented when A is present. With hundreds of rules tested at once, about 5% would pass p<0.05 by luck, so Benjamini-Hochberg controls the false discovery rate.

title: Rule-based recommender
note: A rule fires when its whole antecedent is in the cart. Candidates are scored by confidence × log(1+lift), rewarding rules that are reliable and surprising. If too few rules fire it back-fills with best-sellers, so it always returns k items. That back-fill is why it ties the popularity baseline.

title: Co-occurrence recommender (champion)
note: One matrix product (XᵀX) gives every pairwise count. Each candidate's score is the average conditional probability given each cart item, with optional shrinkage for rare items and a lift exponent (beta) against popularity bias. It uses weak signals that support thresholds throw away.

title: Evaluating a recommender honestly
note: Leave-one-out: hide one random item from each held-out basket and ask whether the recommender's top-k contains it. The 'exclude' option re-scores only baskets whose hidden item is outside the 10 best-sellers. That long-tail metric shows whether a model finds anything non-obvious.

title: Live re-mining endpoint
note: The Mining tab's sliders call this endpoint, which re-runs FP-Growth or Apriori on the cached one-hot training matrix and returns the top rules by lift with the timing.
